reason_for_succession.old_verify_defect: 01_RUNTIME/arpg_item_core.py::verify() used a hardcoded source_kind prefix allowlist (STAGE09_, STAGE13_) plus a pure count comparison between commerce_catalog_snapshots and arpg_item_definitions -- a legitimate additional provider (e.g. STAGE16B_DEVELOPMENT_ONLY) broke resume_world() even when its catalog membership was fully correct, and the count-only check could mask a real one-ref-missing-plus-one-extra defect.
reason_for_succession.new_verify_design: set-membership check: commerce_catalog_refs subset-of item_definition_refs -- fails only with ITEM_DEFINITION_CATALOG_REF_MISSING:<refs> when the subset relation is violated. Strictly more correct: it still catches every case the old count check caught, plus the masking case the old check could not detect.
reason_for_succession.outcome: legitimate additional providers (e.g. the CLOTHES provider documented in this record) can add real, honestly-sourced definitions without fabricating a STAGE09_/STAGE13_ source_kind

runtime_alteration_note: 01_RUNTIME/arpg_item_core.py::verify() was changed, but only as the single, explicitly authorized change carried by the sealed V0_8_0 -> V0_8_1 successor-baseline process documented above -- not an ad hoc alteration of the byte-frozen Stage16A tree.
